correctness.rationale: The proof uses only the stated universal quantifier over finitely supported coefficients, linearity of the synthesis maps, and the ordinary Bessel bound of the reference family. Scaling removes the nonhomogeneous term exactly. The controlled obstruction follows from the polarization criterion for self-adjointness of the controlled operator. The two-dimensional example satisfies the source smallness condition exactly and has a non-self-adjoint controlled operator. The repaired ordinary Bessel constant is attained by a one-atom scalar family.

value.rationale: The finding corrects a named perturbation theorem in two independent but linked ways: it gives an explicit arbitrarily small finite-dimensional counterexample to the controlled conclusion, and it converts the malformed coefficient-dependent estimate into a sharp uniform ordinary Bessel bound. The alpha parameter disappears entirely by homogeneity, and the exact additional commutation condition separates ordinary from controlled Bessel stability.
